title: Transorbital electrical stimulation as a vision restoration tool in patients with significant optic atrophy due to primary open-angle, PEX or pigment dispersion glaucoma. Acronym: VIROA (Vision Restoration in Optic Atrophy)
summary: In this study, we present a new, non-invasive treatment method for patients with primary open-angle, pseudoexfoliation and pigment dispersion glaucoma. Glaucoma is a progressive disease of the optic nerve that, over time, leads to visual field defects. So far, the progression of the disease can only be slowed down by lowering the intraocular pressure. The therapy concept used in the study is a non-invasive electrical stimulation procedure that is used with the aim of reducing visual field defects that has already occurred and thus improving the patient's visual performance. A total of 300 study participants will be randomly divided into three parallel groups. Group 1 receives classic electrostimulation, group 2 nuclear spin-based, individually optimized electrostimulation and group 3 sham stimulation. The stimulation treatment is carried out for 10 consecutive days (weekends excluded).

interventions.name: Classic transorbital electrostimulation is carried out using 2 electrodes placed in the area of ​​the temples. The desired line of sight of the patient is straight ahead. Duration per stimulation unit: 25 minutes

Group 2 receives individualized electrical stimulation based on a MRI scan. Group 3 receives sham stimulation. The majority of patients from group 3 receives transorbital sham stimulation via 2 electrodes placed in the area of ​​the temples, comparable to group 1. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with a known diagnosis of primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG), pseudoexfoliative (PEX) glaucoma, or pigmentary glaucoma (according to the EGS criteria), glaucomatous optic atrophy, and significant glaucomatous visual field loss (Mean Defect >5 dB)
- Age >40 years
- Typical glaucomatous damage to the optic disc and visual field loss in one eye, and either visual field loss or typical glaucomatous damage to the optic disc (or both) in the other eye
- Familiarity with static automated perimetry (at least 5 examinations completed before the start of this study)
- Intraocular pressure <22 mmHg (with or without topical treatment)
- Signed informed consent and willingness to participate
Exclusion criteria:
- Any type of glaucoma other than primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG), pseudoexfoliative (PEX) glaucoma, or pigmentary glaucoma
- Age >90 years
- Visual field defect (Mean Defect) >22 dB or <5 dB
- Deviation in Mean Defect (MD) of >2 dB between the screening visit (Day −28) and the first baseline examination (Day −21)
- Decimal visual acuity <0.2
-  Vision-relevant impairment of the refractive media (e.g., cataract or corneal scarring) that would interfere with the assessment of study effects
- Other ophthalmological causes of significant visual impairment (e.g., vision-relevant age-related macular degeneration or diabetic retinopathy, optic atrophy of other etiology, history of vascular occlusion)
- History of intraocular surgery within 3 months prior to study start
- History of glaucoma surgery or intraocular pressure-lowering laser or cryotherapy within 3 months prior to study start
- Use of more than 4 topical (or oral) intraocular pressure-lowering medications at the baseline examination
- Any change in glaucoma medication within the 3 months prior to study start
- Refractive errors: spherical equivalent greater than +6 D or less than −6 D, cylinder value greater than 3 D
- Patients with documented visual field impairment due to ptosis or dermatochalasis resulting in a visual field of less than 30°
- Other neurological causes of a visual field defect (e.g., history of stroke), except those attributable to POAG, PEX glaucoma, or pigmentary glaucoma
- Women of childbearing potential not using contraception, pregnancy, or breastfeeding
- Neurological disorders (seizures, epilepsy, history of brain surgery, pathological nystagmus)
- Uncontrolled hypertension (systolic blood pressure >160 mmHg)
- Claustrophobia
- Electronic implants (e.g., pacemakers, brain implants) or metallic artifacts in the head
- Psychiatric disorders (e.g., schizophrenia, substance use disorders, substance dependence) that prevent the individual from understanding the nature and scope of the clinical study and its possible consequences
- Inability to understand the nature of the study and provide legally valid informed consent
- Signs indicating that the patient is unlikely to attend the required study visits (e.g., lack of willingness to cooperate, poor compliance)
- Participation in other clinical trials within 12 weeks prior to the start of the study
- Autoimmune diseases in the acute stage (e.g., an acute relapse of multiple sclerosis or atopic dermatitis, or a herpes infection in the temporal region)
- Acute (intra-)ocular inflammation in the study eye or fellow eye
- Treatment with opioids, calcium channel blockers, or benzodiazepines
- Unwillingness to undergo an MRI examination

*The inclusion and exclusion criteria apply to one eye. If the criteria are not met for one eye, the other eye may still be selected as the study eye, provided that all criteria are met for that eye.
